text:
The Halvorsen Strait Ferry Authority formally accepted its new Isolde-class lead vessel into service on 14 March 2031, with a certified capacity of 1,800 passengers and 420 vehicles across two decks.

The figure is set out in the Certificate of Passenger Capacity (Ref. HSFA-IC-0147), which was issued after acceptance trials at Brannock Harbour.

Captain Marguerite Olvanger, the Authority's Fleet Operations Director, confirmed the capacity at the handover.

"The certificate gives us a firm number to plan around," Olvanger said. "The vessel carries 1,800 passengers, and the vehicle decks are rated for 420 cars and other vehicles. That is what we will schedule against."

The ship is the first of the Isolde class to enter service. Its capacity is fixed by the certificate, which records the limits approved following the Brannock Harbour trials.

The Authority said the vessel's vehicle capacity is divided between its two decks.
